summary: Baileys fork pulls libsignal from an unpinned personal GitHub fork
details: @xzvbailss/baileys@1.0.0 declares its `libsignal` dependency as `github:tenka-san/libsignal-node`, a personal GitHub fork with no commit SHA or tag pin. On `npm install`, npm resolves this to whatever the default branch currently points at and runs any lifecycle hooks inside that tree, so whoever controls the `tenka-san` GitHub account can push arbitrary install-time code into every installer of this package independently of this package's own shipped source. The surrounding metadata is consistent with an unofficial redistribution of the well-known `baileys` WhatsApp library: `homepage` and `repository.url` point at Telegram chat links (`https://t.me/XzRzSynxC`, `https://t.me/JustRxVz`) rather than a code repository, and the personal fork is not affiliated with the upstream Signal maintainers.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
